litter mixed with olive mill wastewater as moisture source (no fresh water)

de-oiled cake; oily water to WWTP
Recovered slop oil (crude-equivalent, back to refinery)
Hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria emulsify and consume alkanes, secreting rhamnolipid biosurfactant that also enhances further oil release.

de-oiled sludge slurry (residual HC as carbon source)
Pseudomonas aeruginosa (or non-pathogenic host) fermentation producing rhamnolipid; foam fractionation
Hydrocarbon pyrolysis gases (H2/CO) reduce hematite in red mud to magnetite, which is magnetically separated; tailings are enriched in Sc/REE.

Yield expressed per kg oily sludge: ~1 kg sludge treats ~2-3 kg red mud giving ~0.6 kg magnetic concentrate (rough). Price estimate: iron ore fines ~$100/t. Israel has no alumina refinery (israel_fit 1).
blend oily sludge with dried red mud (sludge supplies reductant + binder)

pyrolysis 600 °C + steam activation of the solids-rich residue
Stored urine reaches pH 9 so PO4 + NH4 + added Mg precipitate as MgNH4PO4·6H2O.
Yield = ~1 g P/L × 7.9 g struvite/g P × 90%. Mg can come from SWRO brine. Very low value per kg.

Commercial in Switzerland (Vuna "Aurin", authorised fertiliser). Price estimate per kg concentrate (~50 g N/kg + premium). Collection infrastructure (no-mix toilets) is the bottleneck in Israel.
biological nitrification (stabilise NH3 as nitrate) → activated carbon (remove pharmaceuticals)
Urease hydrolyses urea to CO3^2- and NH4+; with brine Ca2+ calcite precipitates and cements sand grains at ambient temperature.

Concept demonstrated at Univ. of Cape Town (2018 urine bio-bricks). Yield estimate: brick mass attributable per kg urine (rough, depends on number of feed cycles). Dead Sea end brine as Ca source is the novel pairing.
fresh urine (urea intact) + Ca2+ from Dead Sea end brine (CaCl2-rich)
microbially induced calcite precipitation: Sporosarcina pasteurii urease in sand moulds, 4-6 d curing
Urine supplies all macro-nutrients (N, P, K, S) for microalgae; biomass (non-food) used as biostimulant/biofertiliser.
Yield estimate: 8 g N/L ÷ ~8% N in algae × ~50% uptake. Price P0155 ($5) is feed-grade; urine-grown algae would be restricted to non-food/biostimulant markets (scale caveat).
photobioreactor cultivation of Chlorella/Scenedesmus on urine N/P/K
Free NH3 diffuses through PTFE membrane into acid, forming ammonium sulfate without air stripping energy.
Yield = 8 g N/L × 4.7 kg AS/kg N × 80%. Could feed a green-ammonia/fuel-cell demo instead.
hydrophobic gas-permeable membrane ammonia stripping into H2SO4
Chloride flux salts are highly soluble and recrystallise for reuse in rotary furnaces.

evaporative crystallisation of chloride salts; dioxin-bearing solids to thermal treatment
Reactive alumina dissolves in HCl; controlled partial neutralisation polymerises Al13 Keggin species, the active coagulant.

HCl leach of Al2O3/AlN residue → basification to polyaluminium chloride
Waste aluminate and brine Mg form hydrotalcite; its exchangeable interlayer captures phosphate/fluoride/PFAS.

washed residue → NaOH leach to sodium aluminate
co-precipitation with Mg2+ from SWRO brine at pH 10 → Mg-Al LDH
Fluoride and alumina act as mineralisers that lower clinkering temperature and fuel use.
Price estimate (fluorspar-mineraliser displacement, discounted). Chloride limit in cement kilns is the constraint.

Yield = 25% DM × ~25% chitin (15-40% range) × 0.8 chitin→chitosan. Cost estimate ~$10-12/kg chitosan production cost × 0.05. Commercial (China, India, Norway).

protein hydrolysate; CaCl2 liquor; astaxanthin-rich lipid

as chitosan route + extra purification (reprecipitation, endotoxin removal)
electrospinning chitosan/PEO into nanofibre hemostatic or antibacterial film

lactic-acid fermentation 5-7 d (biological demineralisation/deproteinisation), mild NaOH finish, deacetylation

partial deacetylation/TEMPO oxidation + high-pressure homogenisation to chitin nanofibrils

green extraction with natural deep eutectic solvent or vegetable oil, then concentration

hot-water/sulfite extraction of condensed tannins, spray dry

acid-catalysed self-blowing polycondensation of tannin + furfuryl alcohol (+ diethyl ether blowing)

Fe3+-tannin complexation at pH 3-5 → precipitation, wash, mill (or formulate as rust converter)
Iron-tannate black pigment / metal-phenolic anticorrosion primer

acidified ethanol/water extraction, resin cleanup, spray-dry

solution casting of chitosan/anthocyanin film, drying 40 °C

hot slag tapped directly (sensible heat) or remelt

soda pulping 120-150 °C, wash, thermoform moulded-fibre trays

Yield estimate: ~30% char on DM, ~40% after desilication and burn-off, × 0.8 DM. Price $10/kg Na-ion grade; needs ash <1%.

Yield estimate: SiO2 ~12% DM × 0.8 DM × 47% Si × ~65% yield, as Si/C composite. Price ($30) is husk-derived Si/C; straw silica has more impurities.

acid pectin extraction (pH 1.5-2, 80 °C) then pH/heat or enzymatic depolymerisation to MCP

Yield: GalA ~20% DM ×0.2 DM ×0.77 g/g (250 L scale, Paasikallio 2017) = 0.03. Cost estimate. Opens orange-peel→FDCA→PEF juice bottle story.
whole-cell bioconversion of D-galacturonic acid to meso-galactaric (mucic) acid by engineered T. reesei Δgar1 udh; precipitation by acidification
Limonene loses H2 over dehydrogenation catalysts to the aromatic p-cymene, a bio-route to cresols/terephthalic acid.
Yield: limonene 0.75% fresh wt × 0.8 conversion = 0.006. Limonene recovery itself is commercial (cold-pressed oil); p-cymene upgrading is lab/pilot only.
steam distillation of peel oil (d-limonene ~0.5-1% fresh weight)
catalytic dehydroaromatisation of limonene to p-cymene (Pd/Zn-Cr on support, 300 °C) or in-situ with recovered oil
LM-pectin carboxylates cross-link via Ca2+ (egg-box model) to give edible films/beads for fruit coating or encapsulation; desal calcite fines supply cheap high-purity Ca.

acid pectin extract + calcite fines from desal remineralisation as Ca source
ionotropic gelation: low-methoxyl pectin + Ca2+ (from CaCO3 dissolved with citric/lactic acid) → calcium-pectinate edible coating/film/beads
Glycerol (bp 290 °C) is separated from salts/MONG under vacuum.
Baseline. Yield: 80% glycerol × ~0.85 recovery ≈0.65. Cost estimate from typical refining margin (crude $0.77 vs USP $1.06).
vacuum distillation + carbon/ion-exchange polishing to USP glycerol
Glycerol dehydratase + PDO oxidoreductase reduce glycerol to 1,3-PDO; ~0.5-0.6 g/g theoretical in clostridial pathway.

anaerobic fermentation by Clostridium butyricum to 1,3-propanediol; distillation

transesterification with dimethyl carbonate or glycerolysis of urea (ZnO/CaO catalyst, 140 °C) to glycerol carbonate

methanol removal (autoclave) → soap precipitation by pH
heterotrophic fermentation of Schizochytrium limacinum on crude glycerol → DHA-rich oil

whole-cell oxidation by Gluconobacter oxydans to 1,3-dihydroxyacetone (DHA, sunless-tanning active); crystallisation

classification to filler-grade fine calcite (GCC/PCC substitute)

Te co-recovery from Se refining (Te often co-exists in gas-cleaning residues)

photo-active amorphous Se for X-ray detectors / Se-based solar absorbers
Amorphous aluminosilicate glass reacts pozzolanically with portlandite to form C-S-H.
Baseline/current fate in Israel (fully used by cement). co2 = clinker displaced (~0.8 kg CO2/kg clinker), estimate. Cost = handling estimate.
direct use as SCM in ready-mix/cement
NaOH dissolves the Si/Al glass phase; Na-aluminosilicate gel recrystallises as Na-P1 zeolite with high NH4+/heavy-metal cation-exchange capacity.

Yield 0.57 kg Na-P1/kg ash at ~65% purity (range 0.25 high-purity to 0.98 crude). Cost estimate: ~0.6 kg NaOH/kg ash (Wdowin pilot: 12 kg NaOH per 20 kg ash) partly recycled → ~$0.25 + energy. 10 m3 pilot reactors reported. Product use: NH4+ removal from dairy/sludge centrate in Israel.
two-step alkaline hydrothermal zeolitisation (2 M NaOH, 80-150 °C, 24-48 h)
Fusion converts quartz/mullite to soluble Na-silicates/aluminates; adjusting Si/Al gives faujasite (13X) with high CO2 affinity.

Yield estimate by analogy with fusion Na-A route (ACS IECR 2017, 7.1-yr payback for Na-A). 13X CO2 grade requires purity; price $5/kg is catalogue. Cost estimate: NaOH ~1.2 kg/kg ash partly recycled + fusion energy.
REE in coal ash sit in the glass phase and phosphate grains; alkali roast opens the glass so mineral acid can leach REE, then D2EHPA SX concentrates them.

Yield estimate: ~300 ppm REO in typical coal ash x ~70% recovery; Israeli ash from imported S-African/Colombian/Russian coal, REE content unmeasured. Value per kg ash is tiny unless coupled with zeolite/SCM co-products. US DOE pilots exist.
acid leach (HCl/HNO3) → solvent extraction to mixed REO concentrate
leached aluminosilicate residue (back to cement), Fe concentrate
Cenospheres are gas-filled glass bubbles (density <1) formed in the boiler; they float off in water and serve as lightweight fillers for syntactic foams, oil-well cements, and polymer composites.

Price estimate $0.5-1.5/kg bulk cenospheres (midpoint used, no single sourced quote). Yield 0.01-1% of ash (0.3% assumed; Israeli ash content unknown). Commercial elsewhere → novelty 2. Demo: float test in a beaker.
sinking ash returned to cement use
Waste glass fines dissolved in NaOH give a sodium silicate activator replacing commercial water glass; it polycondenses fly-ash aluminosilicate into N-A-S-H gel.

Yield = kg printable mortar per kg ash (binder ~40% of mortar incl. sand). Price is catalogue $0.5/kg mortar. Cost estimate: NaOH + sand + admixtures ~$0.08/kg mortar. Symbiosis with unrecyclable glass cullet fines (MATMIN-0084). co2 vs OPC mortar, estimate.
mill glass fines <75 µm → dissolve in NaOH (glass-derived Na-silicate)
alkali-activated geopolymer mortar for 3D printing (fly ash + waste-glass activator + sand)
Cutin is a polyester of C16/C18 hydroxy fatty acids; saponification releases 10,16-dihydroxyhexadecanoic acid, which is re-polymerised into crosslinked polyester can linings.

Yield: 25% DM x ~55% skins in dry pomace x 12% cutin (pilot 10-15%; lab up to 32-46% with HPH). Cost estimate (NaOH, heat, drying). TomaPaint pilot 100 kg/h → novelty 3. Israel tomato-paste volume small.
aqueous alkaline hydrolysis 120-130 °C → acid precipitation of cutin monomers (10,16-diHHDA) → bio-lacquer/polyester resin
Lycopene is concentrated in tomato skin chromoplasts; non-polar extraction recovers it as an oleoresin.

Yield estimate: ~0.1% lycopene of pomace DM x 0.25 DM x 70% recovery. Price $296/kg catalogue is for pure lycopene; oleoresin sells lower. Israel fit 4: Lycored (Beer Sheva) is a world lycopene leader → local buyer.
solvent or supercritical CO2 extraction → lycopene oleoresin
Tomato seeds hold ~20-25% oil rich in linoleic acid, extractable mechanically.
Yield estimate: 0.25 DM x 45% seeds x 22% oil x 85% recovery. Niche cosmetic oil.
cold pressing / hexane extraction of tomato seeds
Hydroxy-fatty-acid polyesters are intrinsically hydrophobic/oleophobic enough to replace fluorinated grease barriers on paper.
Price estimate: bio-based barrier coatings ~$10-20/kg (midpoint), no direct quote. EU/US PFAS bans in food packaging create pull. Pairs with pizza-box/food-service paper streams.
cutin monomer → melt polycondensation → aqueous dispersion coated on paperboard
PFAS-free grease/water barrier coating for paper food-service (cutin hydroxy-acid polyester)

Yield as lycopene route. Symbiosis with excess orange-terpene stream (CHEMBIO-0243); Israel has citrus processing plus Lycored. Demo: shake-extract, colour reading.
lycopene extraction with excess d-limonene (orange terpenes) as bio-solvent, then vacuum strip limonene for reuse

saponification (NaOH, aq. MeOH 85 °C) → solvent extraction → crystallisation of β-sitosterol
fatty/rosin acid soaps, wax alcohols, heavy pitch

Yield estimate: 0.098 sterol x ~0.69 mass ratio (MW 286/414) x ~90% conversion. Price estimate $30-50/kg (midpoint) for bulk AD, unsourced. Commercial from soy sterols; using pitch sterols directly is less common. Israel pharma (Teva) is a buyer.
Mycolicibacterium whole-cell side-chain cleavage of phytosterols to AD/ADD

mother-liquor fractionation by vacuum distillation / crystallisation

Yield estimate: ~40% acids in pitch x ~75% to ester. Product quality (colour, odour) unknown; refs only for ester-gum chemistry.

wash screenings → separate wipes/rags from grit
hygienising + drying + fluffing/pelletising of cellulose/viscose fibre fraction

enzymatic/mechanical fibrillation of recovered cellulose to CNF

Yield estimate: 20% DS x 20% char yield. No paper on screenings-derived PFAS sorbents found; analogous sludge-biochar PFAS work exists. Pyrolysis also destroys pathogens.
pyrolysis 700-800 °C + steam activation of mixed screenings to sorbent char
Glycerol transesterifies PET into hydroxyl-terminated terephthalate oligoesters usable as polyols in rigid PU/PIR foam.
Yield estimate: PET ~20% of screenings DS (0.04 kg/kg) + glycerol mass. Price estimate: aromatic polyester polyols ~$1.8-2.5/kg. Contamination tolerance of PU polyols unknown.
separate synthetic nonwoven fraction (PET) → wash → dry

cyclone desliming → flotation of underflow → calcination 600 °C
HCl leach → oxalate precipitation to mixed REO concentrate
P2O5 concentrate, U-bearing leachate, clay residue

Phosphate rock concentrate (~30% P2O5) recovered from slimes

size classification and drying of the fibrous clay fraction

flash calcination 750-800 °C → blend as calcined clay in LC3 cement
Waste 20-25% H2SO4 dissolves apatite and releases REE (and acid is consumed rather than neutralised), coupling two acid/alkaline-earth wastes.
Yield: 300 ppm x 0.4 x 61% (sulfuric/phosphoric leach recovery on flotation tailings, Minerals 2018). Fe/Ti impurities from the weak acid complicate SX.
leach REE and P from slimes with TiO2-industry spent weak sulfuric acid instead of fresh acid
Wool grease (wax esters of sterols/fatty alcohols) emulsifies in hot scour liquor and is centrifuged off.
Moisture blank in DB; yield estimate: ~8% grease of greasy dirty wool x 50% refined lanolin. Commercial scouring practice; low-grade dags usually not scoured.
aqueous detergent scouring → centrifuge wool grease → refine to lanolin
scoured short wool, suint (K salts), dirt

pelletise wool for slow-release N fertiliser / water retention

Yield estimate: 60% clean wool x 11% cystine x 50% recovery. Commercial from feathers/hair in China.
HCl hydrolysis → cystine crystallisation → electrochemical reduction to L-cysteine
Breaking disulfide bonds solubilises keratin; regenerated keratin has cell-adhesion motifs (LDV/RGD) for wound-healing scaffolds.
Yield estimate: 60% clean wool x ~25% extractable to biomedical-grade. $200/kg is specialty; dirty dags need extensive cleaning.

Keratin carries N and S that remain as heteroatom dopants, raising pseudocapacitance and Li-S polysulfide binding.
Yield estimate: ~20% char x ~50% after activation, x clean fraction. Papers on hair/wool-derived doped carbons exist; no specific ref verified.

Spent CIP caustic still carries free NaOH; it hydrolyses keratin into soluble peptides/amino acids for foliar biostimulants, consuming alkali that would otherwise need neutralising.
Yield estimate (solubilised protein + salts). Residual milk organics in CIP liquor are compatible. Na load in product must be checked for soil salinity in Israel.

Price estimate: value as replacement of ready-to-use microbial medium ~$0.03-0.1 per litre (midpoint), unsourced. Israel: Teva, Kamada, Pluri biopharma; Carasso fermentation facility could reuse it.
harvest clarification → heat/chemical inactivation → pH 7 → sterile filtration
use as feed (plus 2% glycerol) for E. coli recombinant-protein fermentation

Yield estimate ~2 g glucan/L. Price uses yeast beta-glucan catalogue ($40) as proxy for fungal glucans.
feed to Trametes versicolor fermentation producing beta/alpha glucans
Residual glucose, lactate, amino acids and ammonium serve as C and N for mixotrophic Chlorella growth.
Yield estimate ~2 g/L dry biomass. Food-grade claims are unlikely from pharma waste, so value is for non-food algae.
mixotrophic microalgae (Chlorella) cultivation on spent media

black soldier fly larvae bioconversion → dry/defat to meal

Yield estimate: ~0.05% anthocyanin of total market waste (only a small fraction is purple produce). Price estimate for indicator-grade extract. Value is the demo, not the volume.

SiC abrasive debris oxidises at firing temperature, releasing CO/CO2 inside the viscous glassy phase and foaming the body into a lightweight insulating ceramic.
Yield: 60% solids less ~8% LOI. Price is catalogue glass-ceramic tile. Israel has small tile production (Negev Ceramics). No Israeli tonnage.
Fines are compatible with ceramic body chemistry at low dosage.
Baseline/current fate (body recycling). Limited by foaming at high dosage.
SiC (density 3.2, very hard) separates from the silicate glass (2.4) by gravity, so it can be reused as abrasive.
Yield estimate: SiC ~3% of dry sludge, 50% recovery. Price estimate: black SiC grit $1-2/kg. Grain size may be too fine to reuse.
hydrocyclone/dense-media separation of SiC grains from glassy fines
The amorphous porcelain glass fines dissolve in alkali and form N-A-S-H gel, and residual MgO adds M-S-H.
Yield estimate. Strength data on this specific sludge not verified.
alkali activation (NaOH/silicate) of glassy polishing fines + MgO

sinter-foam 850-950 °C using sludge SiC as the foaming agent

hot dilute-acid (HNO3/citric, pH 1.5, 80 °C) extraction → ethanol precipitation
Beet parenchyma cell walls (thin primary walls, low lignin) fibrillate easily into cellulose platelets for paints, drilling muds and composites.
Yield estimate: 22% DM x ~25% cellulose recoverable. Commercial (CelluComp Curran).
high-shear homogenisation of parenchyma cellulose into MFC / platelets (Curran-type)
Ferulic acid is ester-linked to arabinan/galactan side chains (~0.8% DM); esterases or mild alkali release it.
Yield estimate: 0.22 x 0.8% x 60%. Can feed vanillin bioconversion.

Yield estimate: 0.22 x 18% x 50%. Price estimate: L-arabinose food grade $10-20/kg (China), unsourced.
mild acid hydrolysis of arabinan → chromatographic separation → crystallisation

Price estimate for research hydrogel material ($50-200/kg), small market. Demo: gel forms in minutes with commercial laccase.
extract pectin keeping feruloyl groups (mild acid)

beet-pulp MFC as viscosity-modifying/anti-shrinkage admixture in 3D-printed fly-ash geopolymer

Fe oxides catalyse H2O2 oxidation of organics.

Hulls are rich in gallic acid, gallotannins and anacardic acids (alkyl-salicylic acids with antimicrobial/anti-biofilm activity).

Pistachio-hull phenolic extract (anacardic + gallic acids, antimicrobial)

cast fish-gelatin film loaded with 5% hull extract
Fish-gelatin active packaging film with onion-skin quercetin

Chloride salts are highly soluble while MgO/Mg(OH)2 are not, so a cold water leach splits the sludge into a potash-bearing brine that the adjacent DSW circuit can crystallise and an insoluble Mg residue.

ESTIMATE: KCl share of sludge not published; 10% KCl assumed (carnallite-derived electrolyte typically KCl-rich). Cost est = leach + pumping ~$20/t. Price = MOP ~$300/t (World Bank pink sheet range $280-350/t 2024-25).
selective leach of KCl/NaCl/MgCl2, return leachate to DSW carnallite/potash circuit; KCl crystallisation
ICL Dead Sea Works (adjacent, same concession)
Muriate of potash (KCl) recovered to Dead Sea circuit
Washed residue is mostly MgO/Mg(OH)2 plus Mg metal fines; calcination converts hydroxide and oxidises Mg to MgO suitable for feed/refractory grade after chloride removal.
ESTIMATE: MgO+Mg share of sludge unpublished; 15% assumed. Chlorinated organics must be destroyed during calcination (check dioxins).
hydration/calcination of washed MgO+Mg fines to caustic-calcined MgO
ICL (Dead Sea Periclase is a sister plant)
Metallic Mg reacts exothermically with water/chloride brine (chloride depassivates the oxide film) releasing 0.083 kg H2 per kg Mg — the hazard (water reactivity) becomes an on-demand H2 source.
ESTIMATE: 2% Mg metal assumed in sludge → 0.0017 kg H2/kg. No reference verified yet; verify Mg metal content before pitch. Also removes the water-reactivity hazard that blocks reuse as fill.
controlled hydrolysis of entrained Mg metal in hot brine/acidified water (Mg + 2H2O → Mg(OH)2 + H2)
ICL / Israeli H2 roadmap; fits hackathon demo (gas evolution, burette)
Mg2+ from the sludge and Al3+ leached from aluminium salt slag co-precipitate as hydrotalcite-type LDH; calcined LDH 'memory effect' captures phosphate, arsenate and fluoride from water.
ESTIMATE: 0.1 kg LDH per kg sludge assumes ~15% Mg-oxide content; cost est includes acid + NaOH. Both partner streams are hazardous wastes - double disposal saving.
leach out chlorides; dissolve Mg residue in acid; partner salt-slag Al leachate
co-precipitation Mg/Al LDH at pH 10 (Mg:Al 3:1), calcination 450 °C
MgO/Mg(OH)2 react with CO2 to form stable Mg carbonates; with biogenic CO2 this yields carbon-negative aggregate/blocks and immobilises residual salts.

Yield est = 15% MgO → hydromagnesite mass gain ~2.3x. Low $ value; main value is turning a 'designated hazardous waste' into an approved construction product (disposal avoided). co2 = CO2 bound per kg sludge (est).
aqueous carbonation of MgO/Mg(OH)2 with biogenic CO2 at 1-10 bar, then compaction
Mg2+ (~2.6 g/kg in 2x brine) precipitates quantitatively as Mg(OH)2 when pH > 10.5; 2.6 g Mg → 6.2 g Mg(OH)2 per kg brine.

Yield: 2.6 g/kg Mg x 2.4 = 6.2 g Mg(OH)2/kg brine, at 100% recovery; 95% assumed. Cost est dominated by NaOH (~1.6 kg NaOH/kg Mg(OH)2 at $0.4/kg). Design-stage plant: specify Mg recovery before outfall is built.
intake brine (no pretreatment needed, already filtered)
two-stage NaOH or dolime precipitation of Mg(OH)2 at pH 10.5-11, settle, filter
Mekorot/IDE; Israel water ministry ZLD planning
Brine Br- (~130 mg/kg) is oxidised to Br2 and stripped; concentration is ~1/40 of Dead Sea, so economics depend on energy integration.
Yield 130 mg/kg x 95% recovery. Cost est > revenue at seawater-brine concentration (2x seawater); included as a reference baseline: likely negative margin unless combined with Mg/Li recovery.
blowing-out process: Cl2 oxidation of Br- then air/steam stripping (as at ICL Sdom)
Li-ion sieves exchange H+ for Li+ selectively over Na+/Mg2+; at ~0.35 mg/kg the stream is very dilute, so value only emerges if hosted on the brine-processing train of a design-stage plant.

Yield = 0.35 mg Li/kg brine (est, 2x seawater 0.17-0.18 mg/kg) x 5.32 (Li→Li2CO3) x 80% recovery = 1.5 g Li2CO3 per tonne brine. Process cost left blank: no TEA for Li from SWRO brine at this dilution; gross value only ~$0.00002/kg so only viable bolted onto Mg recovery train. Research-stage.
Mg/Ca removal (route above) → nanofiltration → ion pre-concentration
Li-selective adsorption (H2TiO3 / lambda-MnO2 ion sieve) or Li-selective electrodialysis on NF permeate
NF concentrates divalent SO4 and partially K; combining with PG sulfate supplies sulfate for K2SO4 crystallisation, pairing two of Israel's largest saline/mineral wastes.
ESTIMATE: K ~0.8 g/kg in 2x brine; 40% recovery as K2SO4 (K→K2SO4 x2.23) = 0.0007-0.0008 kg/kg. Concept stage; no published flowsheet for this exact pairing.
Mg-removal → NF to split sulfate-rich retentate
NF retentate (SO4/K-rich) reacts with phosphogypsum leach; K-Mg double salt crystallisation (schoenite route) to SOP
ICL (Rotem PG + Haifa SOP know-how) + Mekorot
Mixing 2x seawater brine with WWTP effluent releases Gibbs free energy (~0.5-1 kWh/m3 theoretical); RED membranes harvest part of it and dilute the brine before discharge.

UNIT CAVEAT: 'product' is electricity; yield = kWh per kg brine (0.3 kWh/m3 practical net assumed vs ~0.5-1 kWh/m3 theoretical mixing energy), price = $/kWh. Cost blank: RED membrane cost/lifetime not established at scale. Main value may be brine dilution (marine-impact permit).
brine as salinity-gradient energy source: reverse electrodialysis (RED) against treated wastewater effluent before outfall
Sc (90-120 g/t dry) is held in Fe/Ti oxides; dilute H2SO4 dissolves Sc selectively vs Fe (up to 60% Sc with <10% Fe) and SX concentrates it ~1000x.

Yield = 110 g/t Sc dry x 0.65 dry fraction x 1.534 (Sc→Sc2O3) x 0.55 recovery. RUSAL pilot produced 99.9% Sc2O3 (ICSOBA 2019). Cost est (acid + SX) per kg wet RM; TEAs say Sc-only recovery is marginal, integrate with Fe/Ti/REE. Price is catalogue bulk Sc2O3 ($640/kg); RUSAL cites $4,000-5,000/kg for 99.9-99.99%.
dilute H2SO4 leach (<3 M, 1 h) → solvent extraction/ion exchange → oxalate precipitation → calcine to Sc2O3
Hematite in red mud is reduced to magnetite or metallic iron, which magnetic separation pulls out; the leftover tailings are concentrated in Sc/Ti, which improves the economics of Sc recovery.
ESTIMATE: Fe2O3 ~40% dry x 0.65 x 0.8 recovery + gangue = ~0.25 kg concentrate/kg wet. Price = iron ore ~$100/t (62% Fe fines benchmark 2024-25). Cost est from fuel/reductant.
reductive roasting 700-1000 °C → magnetic separation of magnetite/metallic Fe
Iron ore concentrate (from red mud roast-magnetic separation)
Red mud brings free alkali (pH 10-13) and Fe/Al oxides; with reactive aluminosilicate fly ash it forms N-A-S-H gel, using one waste's alkalinity to replace part of the activator for the other.
Yield = dry fraction of red mud into binder. CO2 avoided vs OPC (est 0.3-0.5 kg/kg binder). Israel has fly ash but no alumina refinery; red mud would be imported - low Israel fit.
dry → mill → blend 30-50% red mud with Class F fly ash
alkali-activated geopolymer: residual NaOH in red mud activates fly ash; add waterglass; cure 60 °C
CO2 neutralises NaOH/Na-aluminate alkalinity forming carbonates and dawsonite, lowering pH to ~10 and locking CO2.
Alcoa Kwinana carbonation plant is commercial (novelty 2). Product value is low; main benefit is a de-classified residue and CO2 sequestration (~30 kg CO2/t dry RM est).
carbonation of red-mud slurry with kiln/flue CO2 (Alcoa Kwinana-type) → neutralised mud for soil/aggregate
Red mud's finely dispersed Fe2O3 with Al/Ti oxide supports behaves like a cheap supported iron catalyst; used once-through where conventional catalysts are too costly.
Market for red-mud catalyst is tiny vs 177 Mt stream - volume-limited niche. Yield = dried fraction.
wash → dry → sieve <100 µm → H2 reduce/sulfide
use as Fe-oxide catalyst (methane decomposition to H2 + carbon; coal/bio-oil hydroliquefaction; Fenton oxidation)
spent catalyst returnable to Fe recovery
Spent pickling liquor's free HCl dissolves red mud Fe2O3/Al2O3 while red mud neutralises the acid; the resulting Fe/Al chloride solution is a ready coagulant.
ESTIMATE: 0.3 kg coagulant (solids basis) per kg wet RM; acid consumption limits ratio. Neutralises two wastes. Published concept on red-mud/acid coagulants; no commercial plant found.
leach red mud Fe/Al with spent HCl pickling liquor → poly-ferric-aluminium chloride (PAFC) coagulant
Rendering melts out fat (~15% of carcass); Cat 1/2 fat is legally restricted to fuel/oleochemical use, so biodiesel is the realistic baseline.
Baseline row (textbook). Yield est: 13% fat x 0.95 conversion. co2 est vs diesel displacement.
Protein (~17% wet) is hydrolysed to free amino acids/peptides, which act as N-rich foliar biostimulants for Israeli horticulture.
Yield est = 17% protein x 0.9 → 0.15 kg solids. Regulatory: Israeli MoAg approval needed for Cat 2-derived fertiliser. Cost est (enzymes, evaporation).
Cat 2 rendering or pressure sterilisation → mince
enzymatic/acid hydrolysis of carcass protein → amino-acid biostimulant (EU allows processed Cat 2 hydrolysed protein as organic fertiliser)
Bone mineral is carbonated hydroxyapatite; calcination removes organics/pathogens and gives porous HAp that immobilises Pb as pyromorphite.
Yield est: bone ~10% of poultry carcass, ash ~45% of bone. Calcination >850 °C also destroys prions (relevant to Cat 1 cattle).
calcination to bone-derived hydroxyapatite for soil remediation (Pb/Cd immobilisation) or defluoridation
Israel MoEP contaminated-site remediation (e.g., shooting ranges, Haifa Bay)
Hot alkali hydrolyses proteins and saponifies fats, destroys pathogens (and prions); dairy CIP caustic supplies the alkali that would otherwise be neutralised and discharged.

ESTIMATE: ~1 kg liquid hydrolysate (~20% solids) per kg carcass; price est $0.2/kg = liquid organic N fertiliser ~$200/t. CIP caustic NaOH (1-2%) is dilute - needs top-up; check Na load on soils (prefer KOH systems).
alkaline hydrolysis (150 °C, 4-6 h) using spent dairy CIP caustic as the NaOH/KOH source → sterile amino-acid/peptide liquid fertiliser + bone mineral
Tnuva/Strauss dairy CIP caustic as reagent (sponsor link via partner)
Pyrolysis keeps a carbon network inside the apatite skeleton, giving bone char that removes fluoride and decolourises sugar.
Yield est: bone 10% of carcass x ~60% char yield of degreased bone x 0.6 recovery. Cat 2 animal by-product: bone char for water use needs veterinary approval.
Sulfidic caustic matches kraft white-liquor chemistry (NaOH + Na2S).
Baseline: already practised widely. Yield = ~5% residual free NaOH equivalent (est). No kraft pulp mill in Israel → Israel fit low.
sale as Na2S/NaOH make-up to kraft pulp mills
Naphthenates are protonated under acid and separate as an oil phase; distilled naphthenic acids are sold for metal-naphthenate driers, wood preservatives and fuel additives.
Commercial (Merichem-type) → novelty 2. ESTIMATE: 2% naphthenic acid content (stream-dependent, naphthenic caustics only). Price est $1.2/kg (crude naphthenic acid, industrial listings).
acid springing → phase separation of naphthenic acids → vacuum distillation
Naphthenic acids (crude, from spent caustic springing)

Commercial (Paqell/Shell Thiopaq) → novelty 2. Yield est: Na2S 3% → S 1.2-1.5%. Biosulfur fits Israeli agriculture (sulfur fungicide for vines).
biological sulfide oxidation (Thiopaq-type haloalkaline sulfur bacteria) → elemental biosulfur + regenerated caustic
CO2 (pKa 6.3) protonates naphthenates/phenolates (pKa 5-10) and converts NaOH to bicarbonate, avoiding sulfate brine; biogenic CO2 is otherwise vented.

ESTIMATE: 5% NaOH equivalent → 0.1 kg NaHCO3; 0.08 after losses. Price est $0.25/kg (technical soda/bicarbonate). H2S release must be scrubbed - safety-critical. Concept: CO2 acidification of spent caustic appears in patents but rare in practice.
neutralise/spring spent caustic with biogenic CO2 instead of H2SO4 → NaHCO3/Na2CO3 + separated naphthenic/cresylic oils; H2S captured to biosulfur
Sodium bicarbonate/carbonate (technical) from CO2-sprung spent caustic
Phenolates from gasoline washing are protonated and distilled to cresylic acids for resins, disinfectants and wire enamels.
Commercial (Merichem) → novelty 2. ESTIMATE 2% cresylic content (cresylic caustics). Price est $1.5/kg cresylic acid (industrial).
acid springing of cresylic caustic → cresylic acid fractionation (cresols/xylenols)
Biogenic CO2 at >96% only needs polishing and liquefaction; sells into carbonation, greenhouses and dry ice.

liquefaction & purification to food-grade CO2 (EIGA spec)
Hydrogen-oxidising bacteria fix CO2 via Calvin cycle using H2 energy; biomass ~65% protein.
Yield est = 1 kg biomass needs ~1.8-2 kg CO2 (47% C) → 0.5. Cost est dominated by H2 (~0.3-0.5 kg H2 per kg biomass at $4-5/kg) → ~$2.5/kg CO2. Price is catalogue estimate.
knallgas gas fermentation (Cupriavidus/Xanthobacter) with electrolytic H2 → protein powder (Solein-type)
Strauss/Tnuva alt-protein lines; Carasso fermentation facility

Yield 0.727 theoretical x 0.96. Cost est: 0.136 kg H2/kg CO2 x $4.4 + capex share → negative at catalogue $0.8/kg; e-methanol offtake premiums ($1.5-2/kg) needed.
Mg(OH)2 recovered from SWRO brine carbonates readily with CO2 to basic Mg carbonate, a filler/pharma/fire-retardant product - using two Israeli wastes.

Yield = MgCO3 stoichiometry 84/44 = 1.9 kg per kg CO2 (all CO2 bound). Price est $0.8/kg basic magnesium carbonate (industrial grade, Chinese export listings ~$700-1,200/t). Cost est includes Mg(OH)2 precipitation (NaOH).
bubble CO2 into Mg-rich brine/Mg(OH)2 slurry
carbonation of brine-derived Mg(OH)2 → hydromagnesite/basic magnesium carbonate
Basic magnesium carbonate (light, from brine Mg + biogenic CO2)
Algae fix ~1.8 kg CO2 per kg biomass; COW water supplies low-mineral process water and residual lactose/N for mixotrophy.
Yield = 1/1.85. Cost est from typical PBR biomass cost ~$10/kg → $5/kg CO2. CO2 is not the main cost driver; value attribution to CO2 is generous.
photobioreactor microalgae (Chlorella/spirulina) using biogenic CO2 and whey-permeate (COW water) as water/nutrient base
Tnuva (COW water) + Algatech-style Israeli algae growers
2e- reduction of CO2 to HCOO- at high faradaic efficiency; formate is a liquid H2 carrier and microbial feedstock.
Yield 46/44 x ~0.95. Cost est from electricity ~4-5 kWh/kg at $0.08 plus electrolyser amortisation; no verified TEA attached.
electrochemical CO2 reduction to formate on Sn/Bi gas-diffusion electrodes
First-cut cathode carbon is highly graphitised after years at 950 °C; removing fluoride/sodium salts leaves graphite usable as Li-ion anode feedstock (purity gap 98.3% vs 99.95% target).
Yield est = ~60% C x 0.85 recovery. Cost est for caustic/acid + thermal purification. co2 est vs synthetic graphite (high emission). No Israeli Al smelter → Israel fit 1.
crush → water leach (CN/NH3/H2 off-gas capture) → flotation
alkaline fusion/leach (NaOH) + HCl leach → graphite >98% C; further thermal purification to 99.95%
Leachable NaF/cryolite dissolve in hot water/caustic; Ca2+ precipitates insoluble CaF2, turning the main hazard into a fluorine resource.
Commercial LCLL (Rio Tinto Jonquière) and NALCO lab route → novelty 2. Yield est F 15% → CaF2 x2.05 x 0.8. Price est $0.5/kg acidspar (~$450-550/t).
caustic leach of fluoride + CaO/CaCl2 precipitation → synthetic acid-grade fluorspar; detoxified carbon to cement/steel
Na+ + F- + Al3+ precipitate Na3AlF6 at controlled pH; both wastes come from the aluminium chain and the product closes the loop to the electrolysis cell.
ESTIMATE: 15% F, 70% recovery as cryolite (54% F). Price est $1/kg synthetic cryolite (industrial listings $0.8-1.2/kg).
react NaF-rich SPL liquor with Al leached from aluminium salt slag → synthetic cryolite returned to the smelter bath
Highly graphitic block pieces intercalate sulfate under anodic bias and exfoliate into graphene sheets - no milling/Hummers oxidation needed, so the 'waste form' (monolithic block) is an advantage.

ESTIMATE: 10% mass converted to sellable GNP (exfoliation yields from natural graphite foils typically 10-75%). Concept: graphene from SPL via Hummers reported (Qatalum thesis); direct anodic exfoliation of SPL blocks not found. Demo feasible with a DC supply.
saw intact cathode block pieces → water/caustic wash
electrochemical exfoliation using the graphitised cathode chunk itself as the sacrificial anode in (NH4)2SO4 electrolyte → few-layer graphene
High-graphite carbon dissolves fast in liquid steel, replacing calcined petroleum coke carburisers; only works if S/N/F are low after leaching.
Price est $0.4/kg recarburiser (calcined petcoke grade). Israeli EAF mills (Ashdod/Acre) could use it if imported - Israel fit 2.
use detoxified SPL graphite as EAF recarburiser / carbon raiser
Shell chitin (~20% dry) is freed from CaCO3 and protein, then deacetylated to chitosan (~80% mass yield from chitin).

Calibration anchor #2 (bulk chitosan TRL 9, novelty 2). ASSUMPTION: shells ~40% moisture as received; chitin 20% dry → 0.12 kg chitin → 0.1 kg chitosan. Cost est chemicals + energy. Small Israeli crustacean volume (restaurants; see URBANX-0194).
Astaxanthin esters are bound in the carotenoprotein of the exoskeleton and dissolve in vegetable oil/ethanol.
Yield est 50-100 µg/g wet (crab/shrimp shell literature range); price is catalogue estimate $700/kg (natural astaxanthin value). Do before chitin line - adds value without extra feed.
oil or ethanol extraction of astaxanthin before demineralisation
Ca2+ removed from shells (CaCO3 40-50%) is reprecipitated with CO2 to fine PCC; avoids discharging CaCl2 and uses vented CO2.
Yield est: CaCO3 45% dry x 0.6 dry x 0.95. Low value per kg but converts the largest shell fraction (Ca) into product.
re-precipitate calcium as PCC by bubbling biogenic CO2 + NaOH; regenerate HCl via electrodialysis (optional)
Chitin fibrils (~10-20 nm) in crustacean exoskeleton can be individualised at slightly acidic pH, giving high-strength reinforcing nanofibres and Pickering emulsifiers.
Yield = chitin 0.12 x 0.85. Price is catalogue estimate $100/kg. Market small and early.
mechanical grinding/high-pressure homogenisation (or TEMPO) of purified chitin → chitin nanofibres
The shell's CaCO3 mineral phase acts as a natural hard template; removing it after carbonisation leaves channels in N-rich carbon for supercapacitors.
ESTIMATE: ~0.05 kg carbon per kg shell (organic fraction ~35% dry, ~25% char yield). Crab-shell-templated carbons are reported in academic literature (no verified ref attached).
use CaCO3-chitin nano-architecture as a self-template: carbonise chitin-protein at 800 °C, then HCl-remove CaCO3 → hierarchical N-doped porous carbon
By-product HCl provides the 1-2 M acid for CaCO3 removal; chitosan formulated at 0.1-0.5% acts as a plant defence elicitor for Israeli greenhouse crops.
Yield = chitosan route. Price is catalogue estimate $15/kg formulated active basis. Partner HCl must be free of chlorinated organics.
demineralise with by-product HCl from MDI/TDI plants instead of virgin HCl → chitosan → acid-hydrolysed COS/chitosan plant elicitor
Densification of lignocellulose using native lignin as binder.
Non-graphitising wood carbon develops closed nanopores and turbostratic domains that store Na+; low ash in clean sawdust helps ICE.
Yield est: 0.55 dry x ~25% carbon yield at 1300 °C. Cost est from energy + washing. Stora Enso (lignin-based Lignode) shows wood-derived HC is piloted.
Fungal hyphae bind sawdust particles into a lightweight foam-like composite replacing EPS.
Commercial (Ecovative, uses hemp hurd) → novelty 2. Yield: dry substrate mass becomes product. Good for a Technion demo.
solid-state growth of Ganoderma/Pleurotus mycelium in moulds → heat-kill
Bleached wood pulp from sawdust contains ~42% cellulose; fibrillation yields nanofibrils for coatings, aerogels and composites.
Yield est 0.55 x 0.42 x 0.65. Sawdust gives short fibres - lower quality than chip pulp.
Biochar porosity adsorbs NH4+/PO4 from sludge digestate and slows nutrient release; sludge supplies N/P that bare sawdust char lacks.
ESTIMATE: 0.15 kg char/kg sawdust + equal mass sludge solids → ~0.3 kg product per kg sawdust. Shafdan sludge needs heavy-metal compliance.
slow pyrolysis 550 °C → biochar co-blended/pelletised with digested sewage sludge (Shafdan) → slow-release biochar-mineral fertiliser
Acetic acid, phenolics and furans in the aqueous condensate act as plant growth promoters/biopesticide at 1:200-1:500 dilution.
Yield est 0.2 of dry wood → 0.11 wet basis. Commercial in East Asia → novelty 2.
condensation of pyrolysis vapours → wood vinegar (pyroligneous acid) biostimulant
Hydrodeoxygenation saturates triglycerides to C15-C18 paraffins.

Yield est by mass. Price catalogue estimate $15/kg. Published in literature on waste-oil photoresins; highly polymerised UCO reduces functionality.

Oleic chains form estolides via the double bond; branched esters give low pour point, oxidation-stable lubricants.
estolide synthesis (acid-catalysed FFA condensation) or polyol esterification → biolubricant base oil

Yield est 0.5-0.7 g PHA/g oil reported in literature. Cost est (fermentation + extraction).
fed-batch Cupriavidus necator fermentation on UCO → PHA

Yield 0.85 FAME/kg oil. Eggshell CaO catalyst is well published (novelty 3). Small-scale Israeli municipal biodiesel.
transesterification with methanol using calcined eggshell CaO heterogeneous catalyst
Hydrophobic carbon sources induce rhamnolipid synthesis; UCO is a cheap substrate.
Yield est 0.1-0.3 g/g oil. Price catalogue sourced $7/kg.

ESTIMATE: ~40 g/t Sc in tailings (unverified) x 0.6 dry x 1.53 x 50% → 1.8e-5. Leave as low-confidence placeholder.

Yield est: xylan ~20% dry x 0.8 dry x 0.4 XOS yield. Solid residue can feed a second route.
